Subject: Acme - Post-call recap & next steps (SLO/SLA)

Hi Sam —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our call and proposed next steps so we can align the SLA language with your production requirements: 

Summary of requirements you shared:
- Target latency: p99 <= 150ms for standard (non-streaming) requests, p99 <= 200ms for streaming token completion
- Throughput: sustained 5k requests/minute, bursts up to 12k/min for 10 minutes
- Concurrency: typical concurrency 250-300 concurrent sessions, up to 800 for peak windows
- Streaming: must support real-time token streaming with <=50ms token inter-arrival latency under normal load
- Reporting: weekly dashboard + monthly SLA report; incident notifications via email + PagerDuty

Questions / open items:
1) Confirm whether the p99 definition should be measured at request completion or token-level for streaming.
2) Confirm exclusions you expect in the SLA (maintenance windows, force majeure, customer-side network issues, DoS).
3) Remedies: you mentioned a credit schedule for breaches — are you expecting credits for each monthly breach tier or a cumulative approach?

Attached is an initial redline of the SLA with our suggested measurement language: Acme_Redline_SLA_v1.docx. Neha copied here with technical detail — Neha, can you add a short note about how we measure latency and what we can exclude?

Proposed next steps:
- Neha / Marissa to follow up with measurement specifics and exclusions (by EOD tomorrow)
- Draft final SLA language for legal review (we can aim for a 30-day canary once the contract is signed)
- Set up a shared dashboard in the next week

Sam — can you confirm the above items and which internal stakeholders should be looped for legal and ops?

Thanks,

Thanks Marissa — this is a great summary. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Measurement: we want p99 measured end-to-end on Redwood's side, but we need clarity on whether you include request queuing time at ingress and whether in-flight retries count toward the measurement. For streaming, we care about token-level latency as experienced by the client (so token inter-arrival times matter).
- Exclusions: agree on maintenance windows and force majeure. We also need network exclusions (customer ISP outages) and a clear definition of “scheduled maintenance” (minimum notice period).
- Remedies: we'd prefer a per-breach credit schedule (e.g., 5% credit for first monthly breach, 10% for second) rather than a single cumulative bucket.

Also two asks:
1) Can you confirm whether your reported latency includes time to first token for streaming calls?
2) Can you provide expected CPU/GPU configuration or T-shirt sizing for the concurrency numbers above so our infra team can map expected costs?

Looping in Priya (ops) who will be the primary contact for legal/ops review.

—Sam

From: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Acme - Post-call recap & next steps (SLO/SLA)

Hi Sam — quick technical answers and proposed measuring language for the SLA. Attaching a short guide as well (SLO_Measurement_Guide.pdf).

Measurement (proposed):
- Latency definition: server-side end-to-end latency measured from request ingress timestamp (when request is accepted by Redwood ingress) to completion event when the last token is emitted by the model-serving runtime.
- For streaming calls: we measure both time-to-first-token (TTFT) and p99 of token inter-arrival time over the request lifetime. SLOs can target either TTFT or p99 token inter-arrival depending on your preference.
- Queuing and retries: we include queuing time at the Redwood ingress in the latency measurement. Retries initiated by the client will be treated as separate requests; automatic retries performed by Redwood (e.g., our transparent replay for transient infra errors) are excluded from SLO calculation. We will annotate such retries in the monthly report.

Exclusions (examples we propose to include in SLA):
- Customer network outages between their clients and our ingress
- Scheduled maintenance (with >72 hours notice) and emergency maintenance where we notify as soon as possible
- Force majeure events
- Third-party provider outages (cloud region-level outages) — Redwood will use commercially reasonable efforts to failover but these events will be excluded from SLA calculations

Throughput / concurrency guidance:
- For sustained 5k req/min and bursts to 12k/min: recommended initial capacity is 8 dedicated GPU instances of the XG-1 profile (we'll provide more exact t-shirt sizing once we see a 2-week traffic sample).
- For 250-300 concurrent sessions, plan to reserve concurrency slots and enable autoscaling with a fast-boot pool for cold starts under spikes.

Reporting cadence & telemetry:
- Weekly: shared dashboard (Grafana) with p50/p95/p99, TTFT, throughput, error rates, and token counts
- Monthly: formal SLA report with measurement methodology, any excluded events, and incident summaries

Remedies (proposed):
- Credit schedule: 5% credit for first monthly breach, 10% for second, 15% for third. Credits are applied to the affected month's invoice.

Attaching SLO_Measurement_Guide.pdf with exact metric names and sample queries. Happy to refine wording for legal.

Thanks,
Neha Kapoor
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
neha@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: Acme - Post-call recap & next steps (SLO/SLA)

Sam / Priya —

Thanks for the quick replies. Based on Neha's notes, here's a proposed SLA paragraph we can push to legal (high level):

"Service Latency Measurement: Service latency is measured end-to-end by Redwood from the time a request is accepted by Redwood's ingress to the time the final token is emitted by the model runtime. For streaming requests, Redwood measures both Time-To-First-Token (TTFT) and per-token inter-arrival p99. Reported SLOs exclude scheduled maintenance (>=72 hours notice), customer-side network failures, force majeure, and verified third-party cloud region outages. Transparent infra retries performed by Redwood are excluded from SLO calculations and will be documented in monthly reports."

Proposed reporting cadence & remedies (for legal):
- Weekly dashboard + monthly formal SLA report (PDF)
- Credit schedule: 5% / 10% / 15% per monthly breach tier
- Canary: 30-day canary period post-contract signature where we monitor production and tune thresholds before rolling into formal SLA enforcement

Next steps: if you confirm this language we will have legal prepare a clean SLA and route a DocuSign for signature. I've included a DocuSign placeholder here: https://www.docusign.com/en/documents/abcdef123456 and our HubSpot deal link: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/1234567/company/7654321

If Priya wants to propose any alternate wording for exclusions or remedies, we can incorporate it before routing to legal.

Best,
Marissa

Thanks all — this looks good and aligns with what we discussed. A couple of small requests before legal review:

1) For streaming: can we set the streaming p99 target to 200ms for token inter-arrival instead of 150ms? We need a slightly looser target during our initial rollout.
2) Weekly dashboard is fine; also request a weekly export of the dashboard data as CSV for our internal compliance team.
3) We agree to the 30-day canary and to the proposed credit schedule as long as credits are applied per-breach as outlined.

Priya and I will loop in legal and ops separately (Priya will share any legal redlines). Once we have a clean SLA we can proceed with the DocuSign flow and schedule a kickoff for dashboard setup next week.

—Sam
